source_points.text: Use a dedicated private hcss-utils/documentation-spine repository rather than repurposing adjacent repositories.
Ordinal retry positions are not durable content identity.
Stable job IDs derive from bound run identity, normalized parent path, operation type, and rendered body hash.
The protected main branch contains canonical documents, schemas, and completed compact receipts.
Each live projection uses an isolated branch created from the exact canonical commit.
The immutable manifest binds draft, contract, target, path, writer, canonical commit, and pre-write tree hash.
The deterministic plan records parent-before-child operations, dependencies, and source coverage.
A browser action becomes successful only after fresh persisted Rizzoma readback.
Verified effects are recorded as append-only events with node and rendering evidence.
Checkpoint state is derived from events and can be rebuilt.
A final immutable receipt requires complete structural and visual acceptance evidence.
Resume revalidates bindings and live completed effects before executing missing stable jobs.
Changed inputs, targets, paths, branch heads, or completed effects fail closed as blocked_drift.
A project lease and expected Git head prevent concurrent writers from corrupting evidence.
The authenticated Windows CDP browser remains the supervised mutation executor.
GitHub Actions performs deterministic validation but never receives browser credentials.
Secrets, cookies, profiles, session state, bulk captures, and large binaries are excluded.
The pilot intentionally stops after two of five jobs on a disposable blip and resumes.
Acceptance proves no duplicates, no lost events, complete Hidden state, links, emphasis, structure, and PNG inspection.
Real backfill begins only after the controlled interruption test passes.

children.label: Ledger design
Core decision
Identity over position
An ordinal such as job 18 identifies one temporary plan position, so reordered or inserted work can make the same retry command mutate different content.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete ordinal-retry rejection rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: A stable job identity combines the bound run, normalized parent path, operation type and rendered body hash, so unrelated plan insertions do not rename an existing effect.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete stable-identity derivation rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Dedicated private ledger
The pilot should use a private hcss-utils/documentation-spine repository because real drafts, targets and receipts require durable versioning without public exposure.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete private-repository choice rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: The existing agentic-documents, rizzoma-playback and private rizzoma repositories solve report generation, historical playback and application hosting respectively, so none is the ledger.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete adjacent-repository exclusion rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Repository topology
Canonical main
The protected main branch contains schemas, canonical project Markdown, projection declarations and compact completed receipts.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete canonical-main contents rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Heartbeat and per-operation checkpoint churn stays off main so its history remains a navigable record of accepted knowledge.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete canonical-history boundary rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Projection branches
Every execution starts from the exact canonical commit on projection project run-id, isolating its manifest, plan, events and checkpoint.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete projection-branch isolation rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: After acceptance, the detailed branch is tagged and retained while its compact final receipt is merged into main.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete completed-run preservation rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Durable file roles
Projects hold Research Design, Progress, Decisions, Evidence, source metadata and Rizzoma projection declarations beside stable project identifiers.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete canonical-project layout rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Runs hold manifest.json, plan.json, events.jsonl, checkpoint.json and receipt.json, while schemas and validators remain shared.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete runtime-file layout rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Run identity
Immutable manifest
Before mutation, the manifest binds schema and writer versions, canonical commit, draft and contract hashes, exact target, normalized parent path and expected tree hash.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete manifest binding rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Changing any bound field creates a new run because editing identity after effects land would sever the proof between intent and persisted content.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete manifest immutability rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Deterministic plan
The plan orders operations parent before child and records dependencies, preconditions, source-point coverage and stable job IDs.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete deterministic-plan contents rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Two identical bodies under different parents remain distinct because the normalized parent path participates in stable identity.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete parent-path disambiguation rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Precondition proof
The expected pre-write tree hash proves which live Rizzoma state authorized the first mutation.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete initial-tree precondition rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: The expected Git branch head proves which ledger state authorized each subsequent checkpoint push.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete branch-head precondition rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Recovery protocol
Verified effect ledger
Readback before success
A browser click or successful API response is only an attempted action. A verified effect requires fresh persisted-page readback of the intended subtree.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete verified-effect threshold rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Readback must confirm the affected node, rendered parent path and content hash before the writer may advance.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete per-effect readback evidence rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Append-only events
Each successful event records job ID, sequence, timestamps, affected node IDs, rendered hash, observed path, executor version and relevant fold, link or emphasis evidence.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete successful-event schema rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Failures are classified and appended rather than overwritten, preserving the evidence needed to distinguish retryable interruption from semantic drift.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete failure-event preservation rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Derived checkpoints
checkpoint.json summarizes completed job IDs, the latest verified event, eligible next jobs and current branch head.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete checkpoint summary rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: The checkpoint is disposable derived state because the append-only event stream can reconstruct it exactly.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete checkpoint rebuildability rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Resume semantics
Recovery sequence
Resume reloads the manifest, plan and events, recomputes their hashes, checks the branch head and reads the live target before any mutation.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete resume preflight rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: It revalidates every completed live effect and executes only dependency-ready stable jobs without a verified success event.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete missing-job execution rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Drift refusal
A changed draft, contract, canonical commit, target, parent path or branch head produces blocked_drift instead of reinterpretation.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete input-drift refusal rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: A missing or altered previously completed effect also produces blocked_drift because the old receipt no longer describes the live tree.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete live-effect drift refusal rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Concurrent writer guard
One orchestrator holds the project projection lease, and every checkpoint push compares the expected remote head with the actual head.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete single-writer lease rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: A head mismatch stops the run, while force-pushing checkpoint history is prohibited because it would erase execution evidence.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete history-preservation guard rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Operationalization
Execution boundary
Local CDP executor
The supervised Windows CDP process owns authenticated Rizzoma mutation, fresh readback, evidence capture and checkpoint publication.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete local-executor responsibility rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Its orchestrator exposes process, heartbeat, progress and verified-effect health separately and stops after bounded retries.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete executor-health contract rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: GitHub validation
GitHub Actions validates schemas, hashes, stable-job uniqueness, source coverage, receipt completeness and forbidden artifacts.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete continuous-validation scope rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Actions never operate the authenticated browser, making GitHub the durable control plane rather than the interactive executor.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete control-plane boundary rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Security separation
Credentials, cookies, browser profiles, session-state files and authentication tokens never enter the repository or workflow logs.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete credential exclusion rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Generic schemas, validators and synthetic fixtures may be public, while real topic URLs, drafts, manifests and receipts remain private.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete public-private separation rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Pilot acceptance
Controlled interruption
The first live test writes exactly two verified jobs of a deterministic five-job tree to a disposable blip and then terminates the executor.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete intentional-interruption setup rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Restarting with the same branch and manifest must recognize the first two effects and write only the remaining three.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete duplicate-free continuation rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Receipt gate
The final receipt requires every planned job, complete persisted-tree parity, a passing scoped probe, Hidden threads, surviving links and all three emphasis tiers.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete structural-receipt gate rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Medium-resolution PNG inspection, final tree hash, Git heads and durable screenshot references complete the acceptance evidence.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete visual-receipt gate rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Adoption boundary
The pilot fails on any duplicate node, lost event, unverified advancement, accepted drift, rewritten history or incomplete receipt.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete pilot-failure criteria rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.

children.label: Only after the controlled interruption passes should receipt-backed resume repair the incomplete benchmark branch or manage a real documentation projection.
children.terminal_reason: This sentence states the complete production-adoption threshold rule, so splitting it would only repeat the same requirement.
